intended_object: The endomorphism of the indecomposable projective P_i = Z e_i of the zigzag algebra Z of a graph G given by right multiplication by the volume (degree-two) class x_i = e_i a a* e_i. Taken from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Huerfano–Khovanov.
explanation:
The definition takes the element x_i, which lies in the corner e_i Z e_i, and turns it into a Z-linear map P_i → P_i using the library's equivalence Hom_Z(Z e_i, Z e_j) ≃ e_i Z e_j. The simp lemma `coe_zigzagProjectiveVolumeMul_apply` shows the map sends y to y * x_i, so it is exactly right multiplication by x_i, as the docstring says.

`zigzagVolume` is the class of a backtrack at i. Its value is 0 at an isolated vertex, but that is a documented junk value, and the module only considers graphs without isolated vertices.

This is one specific map attached to the library's zigzag algebra, which is built over a field from a finite simple graph. That is the standard setting of Huerfano–Khovanov. Mathlib has no zigzag algebras, so there is no more general version that this definition fails to use.
